title: Stack Frame With and Without a Canary Under Overflow
description: Interactive SVG comparison of two stack frames under a strcpy buffer overflow — one without a stack canary (exploit succeeds silently) and one with a canary (process aborts on the canary check). Hover the canary or saved return address for details.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity
chapter_title: "System Security: OS, Memory, and Access Control"

educational.topic: Stack buffer overflows and stack canary protection
learningObjectives: Explain how a stack buffer overflow overwrites the saved return address.
Compare a stack frame with and without a canary under the same overflow.
Articulate why the canary turns a silent compromise into a safe abort.
educational.prerequisites: Basic idea of the call stack, return addresses, and fixed-size buffers.

pedagogical.modelType: side-by-side static comparison diagram with hover reveals
controls: Hover/tap the saved return address (either frame)
pedagogical.assessment: Students point to where the overflow stops in each frame and explain why the canary is checked before the function returns.
misconceptionsAddressed: Believing a canary prevents the overflow (it detects corruption, it does not stop the write).
Assuming an overflow always crashes — without a canary it can succeed silently.
